findings.title: OmniSVG: A Unified Scalable Vector Graphics Generation Model
findings.relevance: Current AR-token SOTA. Builds on pretrained Qwen2.5-VL (3.7B and 7B). SVG tokenizer: commands {M,L,C,A,Z,F} as special tokens; coordinates quantized to a 200x200 viewbox and MERGED as one token per point via x*w+y; hex-color special tokens for Fill; <SOP>/<EOS> markers. Trained on MMSVG-2M (1.1M icons ~2.2k tokens, 0.5M illustrations ~8.1k, 0.4M characters ~28k tokens); handles SVGs >30k tokens. Outperforms prior methods on FID/CLIP/HPS (text-to-SVG) and DinoScore/SSIM/LPIPS/MSE (image-to-SVG). Open problems it states: very long generation time for complex samples (tens of thousands of tokens) and failure on natural images. Its coordinate-merging trick and the 30k-token bottleneck are the key data points for GPL.

findings.title: Empowering LLMs to Understand and Generate Complex Vector Graphics (LLM4SVG)
findings.relevance: Adds 55 learnable semantic tokens to existing LLM vocabs (15 tag, 30 attribute, 10 path-command tokens), embeddings initialized by semantic averaging of text descriptions; numbers kept as the base tokenizer's digit tokens. Base models: GPT-2 variants, Phi-2, Falcon, LLaVA. Two-stage training: embedding alignment on 250k SVG-text pairs, then SFT on 580k instructions (SVGX-SFT). Beats GPT-4o/Claude 3.5 on CLIPScore (0.35 vs ~0.30) and human prompt alignment (0.89 vs 0.56); 12-25s inference vs 12+ min for optimization methods. Explicitly documents that tokenizer design dominates performance: models whose tokenizers collapse numbers (Qwen) lose coordinate/color precision, whereas per-number tokens up to 1000 enable decimal coordinates. Directly validates GPL's premise that the tokenizer is the bottleneck.

findings.title: StarVector: Generating Scalable Vector Graphics Code from Images and Text
findings.relevance: Treats vectorization as code generation: CLIP-style image encoder produces visual tokens prefixed to a StarCoder-based code LLM (1B and 8B variants) that emits raw SVG text — i.e., NO custom geometric tokenization, plain text/BPE. Trained on SVG-Stack (2M samples); introduces SVG-Bench (10 datasets, Image-to-SVG / Text-to-SVG / diagram tasks), achieving SOTA at publication with compact semantically-rich primitives (ellipses, polygons, text). Open problems: raw-text coordinates make sequences long and precision brittle — exactly the inefficiency a geometry-aware tokenizer targets. SVG-Bench is a benchmark GPL should evaluate on.

findings.title: Chat2SVG: Vector Graphics Generation with LLMs and Image Diffusion Models
findings.relevance: Hybrid pipeline: an LLM writes a semantic SVG template from geometric primitives; SDEdit+ControlNet diffusion adds detail; dual-stage optimization refines path latents and point coordinates. No learned tokenizer — SVG stays text. Strong visual fidelity, path regularity, and language-based editing, but inherits diffusion cost and optimization loops. Relevant as the 'LLM plans primitives' paradigm: GPL's L2/L3 primitive/shape tokens could replace the fragile text-template stage with a native compressed representation.

findings.title: SVGFusion: Scalable Text-to-SVG Generation via Vector Space Diffusion
findings.venue: arXiv:2412.10437 (project page; same group as LLM4SVG)
findings.relevance: Non-autoregressive alternative: Vector-Pixel Fusion VAE jointly encodes SVG code and its rendered image into a continuous latent; a Vector Space Diffusion Transformer (VS-DiT) denoises in that latent; explicit Rendering Sequence Modeling handles layering/occlusion. Trained on SVGX-Dataset (~240k human-designed SVGs). SOTA-quality editable SVGs strictly aligned with text. Shows (a) rendering/z-order must be modeled explicitly, and (b) joint code+pixel encoding helps — both transferable lessons for GPL's L3 spatial-pattern level.

findings.title: SVGDreamer / SVGDreamer++: Text-Guided SVG Generation with Diffusion Model
findings.relevance: Optimization-based lineage (no tokenizer): differentiable rasterization + Vectorized Particle-based Score Distillation (VPSD) with SIVE semantic primitive control and reward feedback; ++ adds hierarchical image vectorization from segmentation priors. High visual quality and diversity but minutes-long per-sample optimization and over-parameterized, hard-to-edit paths. Defines the quality bar AR-token models are converging to, and the editability/regularity weaknesses that structured token approaches (incl. GPL) exploit.

findings.title: IconShop: Text-Guided Vector Icon Synthesis with Autoregressive Transformers
findings.relevance: Canonical small-AR-transformer precedent: serializes simplified path commands + quantized coordinates into a uniquely-decodable token sequence, trained from scratch on FIGR-8 monochrome icons. Beat image- and language-based baselines on icon quality/diversity; supports editing, interpolation, semantic combination. Limitations: monochrome, icon-scale only, uniform coordinate quantization. This is the closest scale-and-philosophy match to GPL's small synthetic-data transformer — the natural baseline to outperform.

findings.title: DeepSVG: A Hierarchical Generative Network for Vector Graphics Animation
findings.relevance: Root of the lineage: hierarchical two-stage transformer VAE (per-path encoder + global encoder), commands one-hot + quantized argument embeddings, order-invariant path sets, SVG-Icons8 dataset. Established command/coordinate embedding factorization and hierarchy (paths vs primitives) that IconShop, StrokeNUWA, OmniSVG, and HiVG all build on. GPL's L1/L2/L3 hierarchy is the tokenizer-side analog of DeepSVG's encoder hierarchy.

findings.title: StrokeNUWA: Tokenizing Strokes for Vector Graphic Synthesis
findings.relevance: First learned-VQ tokenizer for SVG: VQ-Stroke (VQ-VAE) compresses SVG code into discrete 'stroke tokens' (Code-to-Matrix then Matrix-to-Token), fed to an Encoder-Decoder LLM (Flan-T5). Achieves 6.9% compression ratio and up to 94x inference speedup over optimization methods while beating LLM baselines. Open problems: lossy reconstruction, codebook opacity, limited to stroke-like content. Strongest published evidence that aggressive token compression of SVG geometry pays off — supports GPL's L1/L2/L3 compression thesis, while GPL's interpretable primitive/quadtree tokens avoid VQ's black-box codebook.

findings.title: Hierarchical SVG Tokenization: Learning Compact Visual Programs for SVG Modeling (HiVG)
findings.relevance: CLOSEST COMPETITOR to GPL. Diagnoses the same two failures GPL targets: coordinate hallucination (byte-level tokenization fragments numbers, destroying spatial relationships) and token redundancy in long sequences. Solution: two-tier tokenization — atomic tokens (structured units from raw SVG) + segment tokens (compressed command-parameter groups preserving geometric constraints); coordinates normalized to canvas and uniformly quantized to integer bins; Hierarchical Mean-Noise embedding initialization injects numerical ordering into coordinate-token embeddings; curriculum training on increasing program complexity. Improves fidelity, spatial consistency, and sequence efficiency on text-to-SVG and image-to-SVG. Key difference: HiVG uses UNIFORM quantization — no quadtree/adaptive-resolution coordinates — leaving GPL's ARCS scheme as a clear differentiator. Must-cite and must-benchmark.

findings.title: From Tokens to Numbers: Continuous Number Modeling for SVG Generation (CNM)
findings.relevance: The anti-tokenization position: models SVG numeric parameters as continuous values via regression heads in a multimodal transformer (no coordinate discretization at all), trained on 2M raster-to-SVG pairs + RL with perceptual feedback. Claims >30% faster training and superior perceptual fidelity by removing discretization artifacts. This is the strongest argument GPL must answer: an ablation showing quadtree ARCS coordinates match or beat continuous regression on precision (while retaining discrete-token composability, exact decoding, and pattern compression) would be high-value.

findings.title: InternSVG: Towards Unified SVG Tasks with Multimodal Large Language Models
findings.relevance: Scale-up endpoint: MLLM family unifying SVG understanding, editing, and generation (including animation) with SAgoge — the largest multimodal SVG dataset — plus the SArena benchmark. SVG-specific special tokens and hierarchical-resolution coordinate handling on an InternVL backbone; outperforms open and proprietary models. Shows the field consolidating into data-benchmark-model suites at billions of parameters; GPL competes on the opposite axis (small, sample-efficient, geometry-priors) but should report on SArena/SVGEditBench-style tasks where feasible.

findings.title: Rendering-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Vector Graphics Generation (RLRF)
findings.relevance: Post-training breakthrough orthogonal to tokenization: render generated SVG, compare to target image, use visual fidelity as RL reward (GRPO-style rollouts). On Qwen2.5-VL-7B image-to-SVG: MSE 8.60 -> 1.03, SSIM 79.1 -> 95.1, far beyond SFT; fixes failure modes SFT can't. Implication: whatever tokenizer GPL ships, a rendering-feedback RL stage is now table stakes for SOTA fidelity, and discrete geometric tokens make reward-credit assignment per-primitive feasible.

findings.title: Reason-SVG: Enhancing Structured Reasoning for Vector Graphics Generation with RL
findings.relevance: 'Drawing-with-Thought': model emits a design rationale (layout, primitives, order) before SVG code; RL with hybrid reward (structural validity + visual fidelity + semantics) handles non-differentiable rendering. Related 2026 follow-ons: SVGThinker (arXiv:2509.24299), IntroSVG generator-critic (arXiv:2603.09312), GeoSVG-RL geometry-aware RL for layout-constrained diagrams (arXiv:2605.25447). Trend: explicit structural planning before geometry emission — conceptually aligned with GPL's L3 spatial-pattern tokens acting as a learned 'plan' vocabulary.

findings.title: NeuralSVG: An Implicit Representation for Text-to-Vector Generation
findings.relevance: NeRF-style alternative: entire SVG scene encoded in weights of a small MLP optimized with Score Distillation Sampling; dropout regularization induces meaningful layered structure; inference-time control (e.g., color palette) from one representation. No tokens at all. Strength: ordered, layered, editable output; weakness: per-prompt optimization cost. Reinforces that layer/z-order structure is a first-class quality criterion GPL's representation should preserve losslessly.

findings.title: UniSVG: A Unified Dataset for Vector Graphic Understanding and Generation with MLLMs
findings.relevance: Dataset/benchmark resource (525k items) for SVG understanding + generation with MLLMs; documents that open MLLMs trained on it surpass GPT-4V on SVG tasks; highlights floating-point parameter handling as a core difficulty. Useful training/eval corpus for GPL beyond synthetic data; also SVGen + SVG-1M (arXiv:2508.09168) with CoT annotations and curriculum+RL is a comparable mid-scale text-to-SVG system.

findings.title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Scalable Vector Graphics Processing: A Review
findings.relevance: Survey covering IconShop, StrokeNUWA, StarVector, benchmarks (SVGEditBench, VGBench, SGP-Bench). Conclusions: LLM-based approaches beat standard LLMs, reasoning-enhanced models do best, datasets remain insufficiently diverse, and SVG-specific representation/tokenization is an open problem. Good positioning citation for GPL's gap statement.

findings.title: VecGlypher: Unified Vector Glyph Generation with Language Models; VFig: Vectorizing Complex Figures with VLMs
findings.relevance: Two 2026 datapoints on representation design: VecGlypher normalizes glyphs to a consistent coordinate system with fixed-precision quantized command/coordinate tokens for font generation; VFig shows replacing free-form paths with higher-level primitives (<rect>, <circle>) substantially shortens sequences without losing expressiveness. VFig's finding is direct independent validation of GPL's L1/L2 primitive-level compression.

sota_summary: The field has consolidated (2024-2026) into four paradigms. (1) Optimization/SDS methods (SVGDreamer/++, NeuralSVG, Chat2SVG's refinement stage) give high visual quality but minutes-per-sample cost and over-parameterized, hard-to-edit paths — they are now mostly the quality reference, not the SOTA path. (2) Autoregressive token models are the dominant line, tracing DeepSVG (2020, hierarchical command/arg embeddings) -> IconShop (2023, quantized path tokens, icons only) -> StrokeNUWA (ICML 2024, learned VQ 'stroke tokens', 6.9% compression, 94x speedup) -> StarVector (CVPR 2025, raw SVG text through a code-LLM with image prefix, SVG-Stack 2M + SVG-Bench) -> OmniSVG (NeurIPS 2025, Qwen2.5-VL 3.7B/7B with a purpose-built tokenizer: command type tokens + one-token-per-point coordinates via x*w+y on a 200x200 grid + hex-color tokens; handles 30k-token SVGs) -> InternSVG (ICLR 2026, unified understanding/editing/generation/animation at MLLM scale with the SAgoge dataset). (3) Latent diffusion over vector representations (SVGFusion's VP-VAE + VS-DiT with explicit rendering-sequence modeling) is a credible non-AR alternative. (4) Post-training with rendering feedback is the 2025-2026 step-change: RLRF (render rollouts, image-similarity reward; MSE 8.60->1.03 on Qwen2.5-VL-7B) plus reasoning-first variants (Reason-SVG's Drawing-with-Thought, SVGThinker, IntroSVG generator-critic, GeoSVG-RL) now routinely double SFT fidelity. The most active 2026 frontier is exactly tokenization/number representation: LLM4SVG (CVPR 2025) showed tokenizer numeric handling dominates coordinate precision; HiVG (Apr 2026) introduces hierarchical atomic+segment tokens with uniform coordinate binning, ordering-aware embedding init, and curriculum training to fight 'coordinate hallucination' and token redundancy; CNM (Feb 2026) argues the opposite — drop discrete coordinate tokens entirely for continuous regression heads (30% faster training, no discretization artifacts). Consensus open problems: (a) sequence length — complex SVGs blow past 30k tokens, making generation slow; (b) coordinate precision vs vocabulary size, and embeddings that ignore numeric ordering/spatial proximity; (c) spatial consistency and z-order/occlusion modeling; (d) data — everyone converges on ~250k-2M curated SVGs (MMSVG-2M, SVG-Stack, SVGX, SAgoge, UniSVG) and synthetic instruction pipelines; (e) evaluation fragmentation across SVG-Bench, SArena, VGBench, SGP-Bench; (f) compute — SOTA now sits on 3-8B pretrained VLM backbones, leaving the small-model regime underexplored.
implications_for_gpl: GPL's core thesis is independently validated and now contested: HiVG (arXiv:2604.05072, Apr 2026) names the exact same two problems (coordinate hallucination from fragmented numbers; token redundancy in long sequences) and answers with hierarchical atomic+segment tokens — but uses UNIFORM coordinate binning. GPL's quadtree ARCS adaptive-resolution coordinates are a genuine differentiator; HiVG is the must-cite, must-benchmark closest prior work, and GPL should explicitly frame quadtree coordinates as adaptive precision allocation vs HiVG's fixed grid.

L1/L2/L3 compression is on-trend with strong quantitative precedent: StrokeNUWA achieved 6.9% compression ratio and 94x speedup with learned VQ tokens; VFig (2026) shows primitive substitution (<rect>/<circle> for paths) shortens sequences 'substantially'; OmniSVG's pain point is >30k-token sequences and slow inference. GPL should report compression ratio and tokens-per-SVG against raw-text (StarVector-style), OmniSVG-style coordinate merging, and HiVG segment tokens — sequence efficiency is now a headline metric, not a side note. GPL's interpretable primitives also avoid VQ's black-box codebook, worth stating.

The 5.5k vocabulary sits in a defensible sweet spot: OmniSVG folds a 200x200 grid into x*w+y single-point tokens (40k coordinate combinations), LLM4SVG adds only 55 semantic tokens but leans on per-number tokens up to 1000 for decimal precision, HiVG uses uniform integer bins. A quadtree gives high effective resolution from few tokens — quantify 'effective precision per vocabulary slot' as the key ablation. Also adopt LLM4SVG's lesson: initialize coordinate-token embeddings with numeric-ordering structure (HiVG's Hierarchical Mean-Noise init is the published recipe to compare against).

Answer the continuous-coordinates challenge head-on: CNM (arXiv:2602.02820) claims discrete coordinate tokens are the problem, achieving better fidelity and 30% faster training with continuous regression heads. GPL needs an ablation showing quadtree ARCS matches continuous regression on reconstruction precision while keeping the benefits CNM gives up: exact decodability, compositional pattern tokens (L2/L3), standard cross-entropy training, and compatibility with off-the-shelf LM stacks.

Small synthetic-data transformer is a viable but contrarian position: DeepSVG/IconShop prove the from-scratch small-model regime works for icons, while SOTA rides 3.7-8B pretrained VLMs on 2M curated SVGs. Position GPL as the sample-efficiency/sequence-efficiency play, and validate on at least one public benchmark slice (SVG-Bench from StarVector, MMSVG-2M icon split, or FIGR-8) with standard metrics (SSIM/LPIPS/MSE/DinoScore for reconstruction; CLIPScore/FID/HPS for text-conditioned) so results are legible to the field. The review paper (arXiv:2503.04983) explicitly flags dataset diversity as a gap — a strong synthetic-data generator is itself a contribution.

Plan for an RL-from-rendering-feedback stage: RLRF (arXiv:2505.20793) shows render-and-compare rewards take MSE from 8.60 to 1.03 over SFT and is tokenizer-agnostic. GPL's discrete primitive tokens make per-primitive credit assignment cleaner than raw-text SVG; even a small model + cheap rasterizer reward loop is the established path from 'works' to 'SOTA fidelity'. Curriculum training over program complexity (HiVG) is the other validated training trick for exactly GPL's setup.

Preserve z-order/layering losslessly in the token stream: LLM4SVG attributes hallucinated occlusions to LLMs not modeling rendering order; SVGFusion adds explicit Rendering Sequence Modeling; NeuralSVG regularizes for layered structure. GPL's L3 spatial-pattern tokens must encode (not abstract away) paint order, and ideally expose it as an editable structural signal.

There is an open evaluation gap GPL can own: no published standard exists for tokenizer-intrinsic metrics (reconstruction error at fixed bit budget, vocabulary utilization, compression ratio vs fidelity curves, coordinate-precision histograms). Publishing such a protocol alongside the GPL tokenizer — and running it on OmniSVG-style, HiVG-style, byte-level, and CNM-style baselines — would make the work citable beyond its own model results.

findings.title: StrokeNUWA: Tokenizing Strokes for Vector Graphic Synthesis
findings.relevance: The canonical VQ approach for SVG. Representation: each SVG command becomes a 9-dim vector (command type M/L/C + start point + 2 control points + endpoint); matrices of commands pass through CNN down-sample blocks and residual vector quantization ('VQ-Stroke') into discrete stroke tokens, decoded back via up-sample blocks. Compression: SVG code compressed to 6.9% of raw size (token-level compression described as up to 6.9x in third-party reviews), 94x inference speedup vs optimization-based methods. Fidelity: evaluated with FID, CLIPScore, and Edit Score on FIGR-8-SVG icons with a Flan-T5 backbone (frozen encoder, tuned decoder); surpasses LLM-based and optimization baselines. Trade-off: tokens are opaque codebook indices, requiring a neural decoder — not human-readable SVG.

findings.title: HiVG: Hierarchical SVG Tokenization — Learning Compact Visual Programs for Scalable Vector Graphics Modeling
findings.relevance: The closest published analogue to the GPL Tokenizer. Representation: rule-based atomic tokens (42 structure-tag tokens, 20 command tokens incl. absolute/relative variants, 2,384 coordinate tokens — 795 absolute P_0–P_794 plus 1,589 relative offsets d_-794..d_794 on a 784x784 canvas, attribute/arc-flag tokens; ~2,450 total) plus 500 learned 'segment tokens' that merge a command with all its coordinate parameters via iterative frequency-based pairing under geometric-validity constraints. Compression: 62.7%–63.8% sequence reduction (2.68x–2.76x) vs generic Qwen2.5-VL BPE tokenization. Fidelity: image-to-SVG SSIM 0.896, LPIPS 0.114, CLIP-S 0.957 with a 3B model; wins 58.9–70.8% of human pairwise comparisons. Also introduces Hierarchical Mean-Noise (HMN) embedding init: mean embedding + Gaussian noise + semantic prior + RBF numeric encoding (K=16 bases) so coordinate-token embeddings carry numerical ordering.

findings.title: OmniSVG: A Unified Scalable Vector Graphics Generation Model
findings.relevance: Representation: 6 atomic commands (M, L, C, A, Z, F-fill); coordinates quantized into a 200x200 viewbox and the (x,y) pair merged into a SINGLE token via x*200+y (~40k coordinate vocabulary), so one coordinate point = one token instead of ~6 BPE tokens. Compression: handles SVGs up to 30k tokens (3–4x longer than StarVector's 8.2k raw-code limit). Fidelity: text-to-SVG FID 62.16 vs IconShop 80.84, CLIP 0.3278; image-to-SVG DINO 0.988, LPIPS 0.041, competitive with optimization-based LIVE. Evidence that joint x,y tokens reduce coordinate fragmentation/hallucination — directly supports quadtree cell tokens that encode both axes jointly.

findings.title: CAD-Tokenizer: Towards Text-based CAD Prototyping via Modality-Specific Tokenization
findings.relevance: Representation: sketch-and-extrude command sequences over a 77-token base vocabulary (curve types, structural end-markers, numeric range 0–63), compressed by a sequence-based VQ-VAE (codebook 2048, dim 512, 5-layer enc/dec) with primitive-level pooling — one or a few discrete tokens per sketch-extrusion primitive instead of global pooling. Compression: ~60% sequence reduction vs raw, beating BPE baselines. Fidelity: reconstruction F1-Sketch 94.1, JSD 8.19; downstream text-to-CAD F1-Sketch 77.9 vs 68.8 (CADFusion), Chamfer 26.7 vs 38.5; invalidity ratio 8.38% vs 80.5% for vanilla LLaMA, aided by FSA-constrained decoding. Strong evidence that primitive-level (not byte-level) tokenization plus grammar-constrained decoding is what makes small geometric LMs reliable.

findings.title: VQ-SGen: A Vector Quantized Stroke Representation for Creative Sketch Generation
findings.relevance: Representation: each stroke decoupled into shape (translation-normalized 256x256 raster, VQ-encoded), location (bounding-box quaternion: w/2, h/2, cx, cy), and semantic label — 3 discrete tokens per stroke total. Codebook: 8,192 codes, 512-dim features, 256-dim stroke latents. Compression: an entire stroke collapses to ~3 indices (~13 bits/code). Fidelity: FID 15.78 on Creative Birds vs DoodleFormer 17.48 and DoodlerGAN 39.95; diversity 18.92. Key design lesson: decoupling shape from position before quantization makes codes reusable across locations — analogous to separating GPL's primitive shape tokens (L1/L2) from quadtree ARCS position tokens.

findings.title: LLM4SVG: Empowering LLMs to Understand and Generate Complex Vector Graphics
findings.relevance: Representation: only 55 learnable semantic tokens (15 tags, 30 attributes, 10 path commands) added to an LLM vocab; coordinates kept as decimal text to 2 places (no quantization). New token embeddings initialized from the semantic average of their descriptive text. Fidelity: FID 64.11 (GPT-2-XL backbone) vs Claude 3.5 82.89 and GPT-4o 127.78, CLIP 0.3496. Notable empirical finding: LLMs whose tokenizers enumerate whole numbers (GPT-2 style, all ints <1000 as single tokens) understand numeric/geometric data far better than subword-fragmented number tokenizers — direct validation for dedicated coordinate vocabularies like ARCS.

findings.title: Hierarchical Neural Coding for Controllable CAD Model Generation (HNC-CAD)
findings.relevance: The canonical precedent for three-level geometric tokenization, mirroring GPL's L1/L2/L3. Representation: a VQ-VAE with masked skip connections extracts neural codebooks at three levels — global part arrangement, loop/profile structure, and local curve geometry — encoding each CAD model as a code tree; cascaded autoregressive transformers generate the tree then the model. Fidelity: superior random-generation and conditional-completion quality vs flat-sequence baselines; enables level-wise controllability (specify design at any level). Demonstrates that hierarchical codes improve both controllability and sample quality over flat token streams.

findings.title: BPT: Scaling Mesh Generation via Compressive Tokenization
findings.relevance: Best-in-class geometric sequence compression via hierarchical coordinates. Representation: block-wise indexing partitions the 3D coordinate grid into blocks so each vertex = coarse block index + fine offset index (a direct analogue of quadtree/ARCS coarse-to-fine coordinates), plus patch aggregation around high-degree vertices. Compression: ~75% sequence reduction (compression ratio ~0.26 at resolution 128), enabling generation of meshes with >8k faces. Fidelity: state-of-the-art mesh quality at time of publication. Strong external validation that hierarchical block/cell coordinate tokens are the highest-compression coordinate scheme known for geometry.

findings.title: EdgeRunner: Auto-regressive Auto-encoder for Artistic Mesh Generation
findings.relevance: Representation: EdgeBreaker-style half-edge traversal tokenization that maximizes edge sharing — each new triangle needs only 1 new vertex instead of 3. Compression: 50% (4–5 tokens/face vs 9 naive; ratio ~0.46 at res 128). Fidelity: high-quality artistic meshes at 512 resolution. Lesson for GPL: exploiting adjacency/continuity between consecutive primitives (shared endpoints in paths) is a proven second axis of compression independent of coordinate encoding — analogous to relative/continuation tokens for SVG path segments.

findings.title: Hyperstroke: A Novel High-quality Stroke Representation for Assistive Artistic Drawing
findings.relevance: Representation: VQ-tokenized raster stroke appearance (RGB + alpha opacity) learned from real drawing videos, modeling the temporal stroke-by-stroke process with a transformer. Shows VQ stroke tokens extend beyond geometry to appearance attributes. Relevant as the appearance-attribute counterpart if GPL later adds style/fill tokens, but raster-latent codes sacrifice the editability that GPL's symbolic tokens preserve.

findings.title: IconShop: Text-Guided Vector Icon Synthesis with Autoregressive Transformers
findings.relevance: The baseline all 2024–2026 SVG tokenizers compare against. Representation: SVG paths sequentialized into a uniquely decodable flat token sequence (command tokens + quantized integer coordinate tokens), trained with next-token prediction on FIGR-8. No compression beyond quantization — later work (StrokeNUWA, OmniSVG, HiVG) consistently beats it on FID (e.g., 80.84 vs OmniSVG's 62.16), establishing that flat command+coordinate tokenization is the floor, not the ceiling.

findings.title: FlexCAD: Unified and Versatile Controllable CAD Generation with Fine-tuned LLMs
findings.relevance: Representation: CAD model abstracted as structured text across the full construction hierarchy (sketch-extrusion, extrusion, sketch, face, loop, curve) with hierarchy-aware masked-field infilling for controllable generation. No VQ — pure structured-text tokens. Demonstrates that explicit hierarchy levels in the token stream enable any-level conditional editing with one model; a template for how GPL's L1/L2/L3 levels could support masked editing tasks, not just compression.

findings.title: Pointer-CAD: Unifying B-Rep and Command Sequences via Pointer-based Edges & Faces Selection
findings.relevance: Documents the central failure mode of discretized geometric tokenization: coordinate quantization during sketch/extrude causes topological errors (entities that should coincide no longer do). Solution: pointer tokens that select existing geometric entities (faces/edges) instead of re-emitting quantized coordinates, reducing segmentation/topology error to near zero on a 575K-model dataset. Directly relevant warning for quadtree-quantized SVG: shared endpoints between path segments should reference, not re-quantize.

findings.title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Scalable Vector Graphics Processing: A Review
findings.relevance: Survey cross-checking IconShop, StrokeNUWA, and StarVector strengths/limitations plus SVG benchmarks (SVGEditBench, VGBench, SGP-Bench). Confirms the field's consensus: raw-code tokenization (StarVector) maximizes fidelity but explodes sequence length; VQ stroke tokens (StrokeNUWA) maximize compression but lose editability; structured intermediate tokenizations are the open middle ground — exactly the niche GPL targets.

findings.title: SketchGPT: Autoregressive Modeling for Sketch Generation and Recognition
findings.relevance: Representation: stroke-3 format sketches abstracted into sequences from a predefined finite alphabet of straight-line primitive tokens (rule-based, not learned VQ), pre-trained GPT-style on QuickDraw for generation and recognition. Shows a small hand-designed primitive alphabet suffices for sketch-level tasks — supporting GPL's compact 5.5k symbolic vocabulary over a large learned codebook for the small-data regime.

sota_summary: The 2024–2026 literature on tokenizing vector graphics, strokes, and CAD/geometric sequences has converged from two directions. (1) Learned VQ codebooks: StrokeNUWA (ICML 2024) compresses SVG command matrices through CNN + residual VQ into 'stroke tokens' (code reduced to ~6.9% of raw SVG, 94x faster inference, FID/CLIPScore-competitive on FIGR-8); VQ-SGen collapses each sketch stroke to 3 discrete tokens (8,192-code codebook, FID 15.78 vs DoodleFormer 17.48); CAD-Tokenizer (2025) uses a sequence VQ-VAE with primitive-level pooling (2,048 codes) for ~60% compression, F1-Sketch 94.1 reconstruction, and an 8.4% vs 80.5% invalidity ratio against vanilla LLaMA; HNC-CAD pioneered three-level hierarchical code trees (part arrangement -> profile -> curve). (2) Structured symbolic tokens riding (or training) language models: IconShop set the flat command+quantized-coordinate baseline; OmniSVG (2025) merges (x,y) into a single token (x*200+y on a 200x200 canvas) on Qwen2.5-VL, beating IconShop FID 62.16 vs 80.84 and scaling to 30k-token SVGs; LLM4SVG (CVPR 2025) adds just 55 semantic tokens and shows number-enumerating tokenizers grasp geometry far better than subword fragmentation; HiVG (2026) — the current SOTA and closest analogue to GPL — combines a ~2,450-token atomic vocabulary (absolute + relative coordinate tokens) with 500 learned segment tokens (command merged with its parameters via frequency-based pairing), achieving 2.68–2.76x compression vs generic BPE with SSIM 0.896 / LPIPS 0.114 image-to-SVG at only 3B parameters, plus an RBF-based numeric embedding initialization (HMN). In the adjacent mesh domain, BPT's hierarchical block-index + offset coordinates achieve the field's best compression (~75% reduction, ratio 0.26), and EdgeRunner's adjacency-sharing traversal gets 50% — both confirming coarse-to-fine coordinates and primitive-adjacency reuse as the two strongest compression levers. Consistent findings across all 14+ sources: byte-level BPE is uniformly the worst choice for geometry (coordinate hallucination, token bloat); hierarchical/structured tokenization beats flat; joint (x,y) encoding beats per-axis digits; symbolic (invertible, human-readable) tokens are winning over opaque VQ codes in 2025–2026 because they keep editability and need less training data; coordinate quantization's topology errors (Pointer-CAD) and grammar-constrained decoding (CAD-Tokenizer's FSA) are the recognized remaining pain point and remedy. Typical operating points: vocabularies of 2k–8k, compression of 2.5–4x for symbolic schemes and up to ~14x for VQ schemes, with fidelity measured by render-based SSIM/LPIPS/DINO/FID, command-level F1, and syntactic validity rate.
implications_for_gpl: GPL's 5.5k vocabulary is squarely in the validated sweet spot: HiVG uses ~2,950 (2,450 atomic + 500 segment), CAD-Tokenizer 2,048 codes + 77 base tokens, VQ-SGen 8,192 codes. No published evidence that growing beyond ~8k helps for geometry; OmniSVG's ~40k coordinate vocab works only because it rides a pretrained 3B+ VLM. For a small synthetic-data transformer, staying at 5.5k is defensible and arguably optimal.

The L1/L2/L3 hierarchy (primitives -> shapes -> spatial patterns) is directly validated by HNC-CAD's three-level code tree (curve -> profile -> part arrangement) and HiVG's atomic -> segment split, both of which beat flat tokenization on quality AND controllability. Concrete upgrade from HiVG: learn the upper levels via frequency-based pairing of command+parameter groups under geometric-validity constraints (their 500 'segment tokens' from Structure Segment Learning) rather than hand-enumerating all L2/L3 patterns — a BPE-like pass over L1 token corpora can discover the highest-value shape/pattern tokens automatically.

Quadtree ARCS coordinates are a genuine differentiator — no published SVG tokenizer uses quadtree coordinates yet. The closest precedents strongly support the design: BPT's hierarchical block-index + fine-offset coordinates delivered the best compression in any geometric domain (~75% reduction), and OmniSVG showed merging (x,y) into one token reduces coordinate hallucination — quadtree cells encode x and y jointly by construction. Cite BPT and S2-style hierarchical quadtree geocoding (GeoToken) as precedent when positioning the work.

Benchmark against the now-standard metric suite so results are comparable: (a) compression reported BOTH as ratio vs raw SVG characters and vs a generic BPE tokenizer (HiVG's 2.68–2.76x vs Qwen2.5 BPE is the number to beat for symbolic schemes; StrokeNUWA's ~6.9%/14x is the VQ upper bound), (b) reconstruction fidelity via render-based SSIM/LPIPS/DINO plus command-level F1 (CAD-Tokenizer's F1-Sketch 94.1 is the reference), (c) syntactic validity rate (CAD-Tokenizer: 8.38% invalid with FSA-constrained decoding vs 80.5% without — implement grammar-constrained decoding for GPL's generator; it is the single cheapest reliability win).

Embedding initialization with numeric priors matters disproportionately for small models and new vocabularies: HiVG's HMN init (mean embedding + small Gaussian noise + semantic prior + 16-basis RBF numeric encoding with JL projection) and LLM4SVG's semantic-average init both report stability/quality gains. For GPL's from-scratch transformer, initialize ARCS coordinate-token embeddings so that spatially adjacent quadtree cells have nearby embeddings (e.g., RBF encoding of cell-center coordinates) — this injects the metric structure that pure one-hot vocabularies lack.

Guard against quantization-induced topology errors, the field's documented failure mode (Pointer-CAD 2026): when consecutive path segments share endpoints or shapes share anchor points, re-quantizing each occurrence can break closure/adjacency. Mitigations with precedent: reference/pointer tokens for repeated coordinates (Pointer-CAD), relative-offset tokens alongside absolute ones (HiVG keeps 795 absolute + 1,589 relative coordinate tokens), and adaptive quadtree depth (finer cells where curvature/detail demands, mirroring BPT's resolution-adaptive blocks).

GPL's choice of symbolic, invertible tokens over a learned VQ codebook matches the 2025–2026 trend and the small-data constraint: VQ schemes (StrokeNUWA, CAD-Tokenizer) achieve 2–5x more compression but require large corpora to train codebooks, need a neural decoder (losing direct SVG round-tripping), and sacrifice editability — the review literature (arXiv 2503.04983) flags exactly this trade-off. A hybrid worth testing later: keep L1 symbolic, and distill only L3 spatial patterns into a small learned codebook once synthetic data volume permits, following CAD-Tokenizer's primitive-level pooling.

Adopt curriculum training on program complexity (HiVG progressively increases SVG program complexity during training) — it is reported to stabilize learning of executable structured sequences and is essentially free to implement with a synthetic data generator, which can emit difficulty-graded samples on demand. Combined with adjacency-aware compression (EdgeRunner's 50% from sharing edges suggests continuation tokens for connected path segments), these are the highest-leverage, lowest-cost additions from the current literature.

findings.title: xVal: A Continuous Number(ical) Encoding / Tokenization for Scientific Language Models
findings.venue: arXiv 2310.02989; NeurIPS 2023 AI4Science workshop; Polymathic AI
findings.relevance: Encodes any real number as a single [NUM] token whose embedding is scaled by the value, decoded with an MSE number head. End-to-end continuous, more token-efficient than digit-BPE, better OOD interpolation on scientific data. Weakness for GPL: limited precision for exact coordinates (only scalar magnitude), best as a continuous offset head, not for high-precision absolute coordinates.

findings.title: FoNE: Precise Single-Token Number Embeddings via Fourier Features
findings.relevance: Maps each number to one token via Fourier features (2 embedding dims per digit), preserving exact value with no fragmentation. Beats digit-wise and subword embeddings on add/sub/mul, 99%+ accuracy with 64x less data and 3-6x fewer tokens. Currently the strongest published 'single-token exact number' scheme — directly applicable to embedding GPL's ARCS coordinate tokens (deterministic Fourier init instead of random embeddings).

findings.title: Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens
findings.relevance: Tokenizer-free: entropy-based dynamic patching over raw bytes; matches/outperforms BPE at 7-8B scale with up to 50% inference FLOP savings and better robustness/digit handling. But crossover only appears at large scale — at small-model, small-data regimes like GPL, BPE-class fixed vocabularies still win on compute. Idea worth borrowing: allocate more tokens where geometry entropy is high.

findings.title: SuperBPE: Space Travel for Language Models
findings.relevance: Superword tokens that cross whitespace: up to 33% fewer tokens at fixed vocab, +4% avg / +8.2% MMLU at 8B, 27% cheaper inference. Validates GPL's L2/L3 approach — at fixed vocabulary, learning multi-unit tokens (multi-coordinate/multi-command motifs) is strictly better than per-symbol BPE. A 'curriculum' BPE (subunits first, motifs second) is transferable.

findings.title: H-Net: Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling
findings.relevance: Learned, differentiable chunk boundaries over raw bytes; byte-level H-Net matches/exceeds BPE transformers at >1B params, ~4.5-5 bytes/chunk emerging without supervision; multi-stage hierarchy matches token Transformer of twice its size. Conceptually mirrors GPL's L1/L2/L3 hierarchy — supports the idea that hierarchical compression is the right inductive bias; a learned boundary predictor could automate L3 spatial-pattern mining.

findings.title: Transformers Can Do Arithmetic with the Right Embeddings (Abacus Embeddings)
findings.relevance: Digit-significance positional embeddings (position within the number, random offset) give 6x length generalization (to 120-digit addition, 97%+); input injection cuts errors another 50%. If GPL ever emits raw digits, abacus-style significance encoding is mandatory; analog for GPL — encode quadtree depth/significance level of each ARCS symbol as a dedicated positional channel.

findings.title: Tokenization Counts: the Impact of Tokenization on Arithmetic in Frontier LLMs
findings.relevance: Left-to-right 3-digit BPE chunking causes systematic arithmetic errors; right-to-left (significance-aligned) chunking largely fixes them. Lesson: chunk boundaries must align with numeric significance — GPL's quadtree ARCS (most-significant cell first, fixed alignment) already satisfies this; never mix variable-length digit chunks.

findings.title: Regress, Don't Guess — Number Token Loss (NTL)
findings.relevance: Adds an Lp/Wasserstein regression loss over numeric token values on top of cross-entropy; drop-in, no architecture change, consistent gains on math tasks. Directly portable to GPL: ARCS cells have known spatial values, so add a distance-weighted auxiliary loss penalizing predictions by geometric distance — cheap win for a small synthetic transformer.

findings.title: HiVG: Hierarchical SVG Tokenization — Learning Compact Visual Programs
findings.relevance: Closest competitor to GPL. Atomic tokens (commands/coordinates) + segment tokens (compressed command-parameter groups), Hierarchical Mean-Noise embedding initialization injecting numeric ordering, curriculum training. Explicitly shows generic/digit-BPE tokenizers cause coordinate hallucination and that geometry-aware hierarchical tokens beat them on fidelity, spatial consistency, sequence efficiency.

findings.title: LLM4SVG: Empowering LLMs to Understand and Generate Complex Vector Graphics
findings.relevance: Learnable semantic SVG tokens; ablations show coordinate accuracy depends heavily on how the base tokenizer chunks numbers (Qwen-style merged number tokens hurt coordinates). Confirms digit-BPE inherited from text LLMs is the bottleneck GPL is built to remove; SVGX-SFT-1M dataset reusable for evaluation.

findings.title: ByteFlow: Language Modeling through Adaptive Byte Compression without a Tokenizer
findings.relevance: Compression-driven (coding-rate) segmentation of byte streams; outperforms BPE transformers and prior byte-level models. With H-Net/BLT, establishes that 2026 tokenizer-free SOTA discovers BPE-like units automatically — but at compute budgets far above GPL's regime.

findings.title: Value-Aware Numerical Representations for Transformer LMs / DriveCode numeric encoding
findings.relevance: 2026 line of work: dedicated value-aware embeddings and number projectors into hidden space (DriveCode for trajectories) beat digit tokenization for continuous trajectory coordinates. Shows the field is converging on hybrid discrete-token + continuous-value heads for coordinates — applicable to GPL fine-offset prediction within quadtree cells.

sota_summary: Consensus across 2024-2026: vanilla digit-BPE is the worst widely used option for numbers and coordinates, but vocabulary-free byte-level models are not the fix at small scale. The strongest current results favor structured single-token number representations: FoNE (ICLR 2026) makes each number one token via Fourier-feature embeddings (2 dims/digit) and beats digit-wise/subword tokenization with up to 64x data and 3-6x token efficiency; xVal handles continuous magnitudes well (interpolation-friendly, MSE-decoded) but lacks digit precision. Where discrete tokens are kept, three orthogonal fixes give most of the gain: significance-aligned chunking (right-to-left grouping; arXiv 2402.14903), abacus digit-position embeddings (6x length generalization; NeurIPS 2024), and Number Token Loss regression on top of cross-entropy (ICML 2025, drop-in). Tokenizer-free architectures (BLT, H-Net, ByteFlow, H-Net++) now match or beat BPE — but only at roughly >=1B params and large data, with chunks self-organizing to ~4.5-5 bytes; at small scale fixed geometry-aware vocabularies still win. At fixed vocab, SuperBPE (COLM 2025) shows multi-word/super tokens beat plain BPE (+4% avg, 27% inference savings), supporting hierarchical motif compression. For SVG/coordinates specifically, HiVG (2026) and LLM4SVG (CVPR 2025) show generic numeric tokenization causes coordinate hallucination, and that hierarchical geometry-aware tokens (atomic + segment, value-ordered embedding init, curriculum) beat digit-BPE on fidelity, spatial consistency, and sequence length. Net: best practice for coordinates = single discrete coordinate tokens with value-aware (Fourier/mean-noise) embeddings, hierarchical motif tokens for compression, plus a regression-like auxiliary loss; tokenizer-free is the wrong end of the trade-off at GPL's scale.
implications_for_gpl: GPL's core design is validated: quadtree ARCS coordinates as discrete single tokens + L1/L2/L3 motif compression is exactly the direction HiVG (atomic+segment tokens), SuperBPE (super tokens at fixed vocab), and H-Net (hierarchy beats flat) prove out; HiVG is the closest prior art and should be cited and benchmarked against.

Highest-leverage easy upgrade: value-aware embedding initialization for ARCS coordinate tokens — initialize embeddings with FoNE-style Fourier features of cell center (sin/cos at quadtree-period frequencies, ~2 dims per level) or HiVG mean-noise ordering, so spatially adjacent cells get adjacent embeddings instead of i.i.d. random ones; near-zero cost, big data-efficiency win on a 5.5k vocab small model.

Add a Number Token Loss analog: an auxiliary loss weighting wrong coordinate predictions by geometric (L2 grid) distance between predicted and true cell, layered on cross-entropy (ICML 2025 NTL is drop-in and works for small models); also adopt HiVG's coordinate-hallucination/spatial-consistency metrics for eval.

For sub-cell precision, prefer a hybrid head over deeper quadtrees: discrete ARCS token for the cell + small xVal/DriveCode-style continuous regression head for the residual offset — continuous heads interpolate well, discrete tokens stay precise; avoids vocab blowup beyond 5.5k.

Keep significance alignment guarantees: ARCS coarse-to-fine ordering already mirrors significance-aligned chunking; never variable-width-chunk coordinates; optionally add an abacus-style positional channel encoding quadtree depth and slot index within each primitive (input injection helps small models generalize to longer shapes).

Do not switch to tokenizer-free (BLT/H-Net/ByteFlow): gains appear at >=1B params and large data, not a small synthetic-data transformer; but H-Net's learned boundary/entropy-driven chunking can be borrowed offline as a data-driven discovery tool for L2/L3 motif boundaries instead of purely greedy BPE counts.

SuperBPE's curriculum trick transfers: train motif vocab in stages (L1 first, freeze, then allow L2/L3 superwords across primitive boundaries) — this beats one-shot BPE at equal vocab and matches GPL's compression rationale (~33% token reduction reported).

Don't grow vocab with raw digit tokens (10-1000 number tokens): both Pythia numeral-system study (base-10 most data-efficient) and frequency-bias results say frequency-imbalanced number tokens hurt; quadtree cell tokens with uniform synthetic coverage avoid this failure mode entirely.

findings.title: VGBench: Evaluating Large Language Models on Vector Graphics Understanding and Generation (Zou et al.)
findings.relevance: EXISTS. 4,279 understanding QA pairs + 5,845 generation samples across SVG/TikZ/Graphviz. Found LLMs are weakest on low-level SVG — exactly the gap a geometry-aware tokenizer targets. Standard zero-/few-shot eval (CLIPScore, FID, QA accuracy) usable for GPL downstream tests. Project: https://vgbench.github.io, ACL: https://aclanthology.org/2024.emnlp-main.213.pdf

findings.title: SVG-Bench (introduced in StarVector, Rodriguez et al.)
findings.relevance: EXISTS as part of StarVector. Image-to-SVG benchmark spanning SVG-Stack/SVG-Fonts/SVG-Icons/SVG-Emoji with MSE, SSIM, CLIP, DinoScore metrics. Also introduced SVG-Stack (2.1M train / 108k val / 5.7k test, permissively licensed) — the de facto pretraining corpus. Note a separate unrelated community 'SVGBench' exists at github.com/johnbean393/SVGBench. CVF PDF: openaccess.thecvf.com CVPR2025; dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/starvector/svg-stack

findings.title: SVGEditBench (Nishina & Matsui)
findings.relevance: EXISTS. 6 deterministic editing tasks (color, contour, crop, rotate, transform, compress) with MSE-based scoring. Cheap, automatic — well suited as a downstream probe of whether GPL's L1/L2 tokens preserve editability. Code: https://github.com/mti-lab/SVGEditBench

findings.title: SVGEditBench V2: A Benchmark for Instruction-based SVG Editing
findings.relevance: EXISTS. 1,683 triplets (original SVG, ground-truth edited SVG, GPT-4o prompt) from emoji datasets. Instruction-following SVG editing protocol; complements V1's synthetic edits.

findings.title: FIGR-8-SVG
findings.relevance: EXISTS. ~1.5M monochrome icons, 17,375 classes. Canonical small-shape SVG corpus used by DeepSVG, IconShop, StrokeNUWA. Ideal real-data complement to GPL's synthetic training; closest in scale/simplicity to a 5.5k-vocab small transformer regime.

findings.title: MMSVG-2M / MMSVG-Bench (OmniSVG, Yang et al.)
findings.relevance: EXISTS. 2M annotated SVGs (Icon/Illustration/Character) + standardized conditional-generation protocol. OmniSVG also tokenizes commands+coordinates into discrete tokens (coordinates as single tokens on a grid) — the nearest large-scale baseline to compare GPL's quadtree ARCS coordinates against. Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/OmniSVG/MMSVG-Icon

findings.title: SVGenius: Benchmarking LLMs in SVG Understanding, Editing and Generation
findings.relevance: EXISTS. 2,377 queries, 8 task categories, 18 metrics, complexity-stratified — the most complete eval suite for low-complexity-to-high-complexity scaling claims, matching GPL's L1/L2/L3 hierarchy framing. https://zju-real.github.io/SVGenius

findings.title: VectorGym: A Multitask Benchmark for SVG Code Generation, Sketching, and Editing (Rodriguez et al., ServiceNow)
findings.relevance: VERIFIED REAL (arXiv abs page, HF papers, OpenReview, HF dataset all confirm). Juan Rodriguez et al. (StarVector authors). Four tasks with expert human annotations: VG-Sketch (Sketch2SVG), VG-Edit (multi-step edits), VG-Text, VG-Cap; VLM-as-judge metric validated by human correlation; GRPO multi-task RL gets Qwen3-VL 8B to GPT-4o level. Newest, hardest target suite. Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ServiceNow/VectorGym

findings.title: HiVG: Hierarchical SVG Tokenization — Learning Compact Visual Programs (Xing et al.)
findings.relevance: VERIFIED REAL — and the closest direct competitor to GPL. Atomic tokens + geometry-constrained segment tokens compressing command-parameter groups; Hierarchical Mean-Noise embedding init; curriculum training; evaluated on text-to-SVG and image-to-SVG fidelity/spatial-consistency/sequence-efficiency. From the SVGDreamer group. Caution: name collides with HiVG visual grounding (arXiv 2404.13400, 2024). Project: https://hy-hivg.github.io

findings.title: 'GPL tokenizer' in the literature
findings.relevance: DOES NOT EXIST in literature. Web + arXiv + HF paper searches return no paper, dataset, or repo by that name (only AGG svg_path_tokenizer code and unrelated GCP-VQVAE/GPSToken). The name is free for the user's project, but is unfortunate due to GPL-license connotation — consider renaming for publication.

findings.title: From Tokens to Numbers: Continuous Number Modeling for SVG Generation (Ogezi et al.)
findings.relevance: EXISTS. The opposing camp: models coordinates as continuous values instead of tokens; 30% faster training on 2M raster-to-SVG pairs; merged corpus = SVG-Stack 2.28M + SVGX 257k + MMSVG-Icon 1.16M, deduped to 2.44M. GPL must argue discrete quadtree ARCS beats continuous regression.

findings.title: Beyond Text Compression: Evaluating Tokenizers Across Scales
findings.relevance: Tokenizer impact methodology: intrinsic metrics (compression, fertility, Zipf-inspired stats) correlate only partially with downstream; proposes cheap proxies cutting extrinsic eval cost 85%. Template for GPL's evaluation protocol.

findings.title: Tokenizer Choice For LLM Training: Negligible or Crucial?
findings.relevance: Canonical extrinsic protocol: train identical small models varying only tokenizer, compare downstream suite + cost. Exactly the controlled-experiment design GPL needs at small-transformer scale.

findings.title: Unpacking Tokenization: Evaluating Text Compression and its Correlation with Model Performance
findings.relevance: Shows compression correlates with downstream performance but is insufficient alone — GPL cannot rest its claim on compression ratio; needs rendered-fidelity and task metrics.

findings.title: StrokeNUWA: Tokenizing Strokes for Vector Graphic Synthesis
findings.relevance: VQ-VAE stroke tokens, ~6.9x shorter sequences, 94x speedup — prior art for learned vector tokens and the compression-ratio baseline GPL will be compared to, alongside IconShop (arXiv:2304.14400) and CAD-Tokenizer (arXiv:2509.21150).

sota_summary: SOTA (mid-2026): SVG modeling has moved from differentiable rendering to autoregressive program synthesis, and tokenization is now an explicit research front. HiVG (arXiv:2604.05072, Apr 2026) is the direct SOTA in geometry-aware SVG tokenization — atomic + geometry-constrained segment tokens, embedding init priors, curriculum training — beating byte-level BPE on fidelity, spatial consistency, and sequence efficiency. The continuous camp (Continuous Number Modeling, arXiv:2602.02820) attacks the same coordinate-fragmentation problem by removing coordinate tokens entirely. Benchmarks have stratified: VGBench (EMNLP'24, understanding+generation), SVGEditBench/V2 (automatic editing), SVG-Bench/StarVector (CVPR'25, image-to-SVG), MMSVG-Bench (NeurIPS'25, 2M assets), SVGenius (ACM MM'25, complexity-stratified, 18 metrics), and VectorGym (Feb 2026, ServiceNow/Rodriguez — verified real, human-annotated Sketch2SVG/Edit/Text/Cap with VLM-as-judge). Big corpora are settled: SVG-Stack 2.1M, MMSVG-2M, MMSVG-Icon 1.16M, SVGX 257k, FIGR-8-SVG 1.5M; recent works train on ~2.4M deduped merged. Verdicts: VGBench, SVG-Bench, SVGEditBench, FIGR-8-SVG, MMSVG, VectorGym (Rodriguez et al.), HiVG all exist; "GPL tokenizer" does not exist in the literature. Tokenizer papers establish impact via paired intrinsic (compression/fertility/vocab stats) + extrinsic protocols: identical small models differing only in tokenizer, evaluated on a downstream task suite; compression alone is established as insufficient evidence.
implications_for_gpl: Name: 'GPL Tokenizer' is unclaimed but collides with the GPL license; consider renaming before any release. The concept is no longer novel in isolation — HiVG (Apr 2026, same thesis of structured atomic + compressed geometric tokens) must be cited and beaten or differentiated; quadtree ARCS hierarchical coordinates and explicit L3 spatial-pattern tokens are the plausible differentiators since HiVG has no quadtree multiresolution coordinates.

Evaluation protocol: copy the tokenizer-literature standard — train identical small transformers varying only tokenizer (BPE baseline, OmniSVG-style fixed grid, HiVG if reproducible, CNM continuous, GPL) and report intrinsic (tokens/SVG, vocab utilization, fertility) plus downstream rendered fidelity (MSE/SSIM/CLIP/DINO). Compression ratio alone will not be accepted as impact (per arXiv:2403.06265, 2506.03101).

Downstream suite: SVGEditBench V1/V2 (automatic, cheap, fits small models), VGBench-SVG and SVGenius low/medium complexity tiers, MMSVG-Bench icons. VectorGym is the headline 2026 target but is human-annotation hard; report it only if scaling beyond toy models.

Data: synthetic-only training is a weakness reviewers will flag — add FIGR-8-SVG (1.5M monochrome icons, matches small-vocab regime) or SVG-Stack/MMSVG-Icon subsets to show real-SVG generalization; standard preprocessing pipelines exist in DeepSVG/IconShop repos.

5.5k vocab is well-positioned: smaller than OmniSVG's coordinate vocab and far smaller than byte BPE; frame it as compute-frugal, fixed-precision quadtree coordinates with hierarchical refinement, contrasting both with HiVG's segment tokens and CNM's continuous regression. Quantify reconstruction error vs vocab size to defend discreteness against CNM.

Strongest available impact story: show GPL reduces coordinate hallucination and sequence length (the failure modes HiVG names) at 10-100x less training compute, then ablate L1/L2/L3 — hierarchical ablations are what got HiVG and StrokeNUWA accepted.
